name: Mizuchi
title: Mizuchi, el Gran Koi del Lago Kohan: the koi that climbs the waterfall
pitch:
Mizuchi is the 'Nushi' (ancient lord) of Lake Kohan. It is a 7.5 m Tancho-Kohaku koi spirit that swims through the air over the shrine platform. The platform sits at the foot of a horseshoe waterfall that the koi has tried to climb for 300 years. The fight retells a real Japanese legend, the Dragon Gate ('koi no takinobori': a koi that climbs the waterfall becomes a dragon). That makes the waterfall more than scenery: it is what the boss wants, it drives the phase-2 transformation and it is the ending. The Kurokage clan drove the Water Seal into the koi's back as an iron stake. The fight is about freeing the koi, not killing it. When it is beaten, Kaito pulls the stake out, the koi climbs the falls and rises as a golden dragon. That dragon echoes the yellow dragon of the Bandana Spirit bar.

Design pillars, all checked in a Blender prototype rendered from the real game camera:
1. It reads from above. Koi are bred to be admired from above. A single red disc (the 'tancho' marking) on the white head always shows where the head is, and so where the bite is coming from.
2. It moves like a real fish. The wind-up is a C-start, the strike is an S-snap, it swims with a travelling wave and it flops when beached (the exhausted state). These are real fish movements on a creature that is clearly not real, which is what the user asked for.
3. It uses one consistent set of cues. Parryable attacks get a white glint and a water chime exactly 0.33 s before contact. Attacks you must dodge get a red ground marking and a taiko hit at least 0.9 s ahead.
4. The waterfall is pulled into the gameplay frame. I measured that a waterfall standing behind the arena is invisible from the current gameplay camera. So the plan uses a horseshoe of falls wrapped around the arena, mist and spray over the deck, attacks that use the falls' water, a camera turn and short 'look up' camera moments.

Name: 'Mizuchi' is a real Japanese river-dragon spirit, which is what the koi is meant to become. Keeping the name means no changes to save flags (boss_mizuchi), the portal or world_plan, and the existing name finally fits.
lore:
The village: the fishermen of Kohanoie built the octagonal shrine platform in the middle of Lake Kohan to watch the Takinobori-matsuri (waterfall-climbing festival). Every full moon they lit the platform's lanterns and beat drums while the Great Koi tried to climb the Kohan Falls. Every year it fell a few metres short. It never stopped trying. To the village it stands for perseverance.

The crime: the Kurokage clan needed a guardian for each of the three seals that lock the dojo gate. At the lake they drove the Water Seal, as an iron stake, into the koi's back. The seal is the same medallion as the key_seal_lake prop (wave relief, gold rim), at 2.5x scale. It is wrapped in a shimenawa rope and a black clan talisman (a clan crest, never kanji). Since then the koi cannot climb. The corruption spreads out from the stake and turns its scales black when it is enraged. The lake has gone dark and the lanterns are out. The fishermen stopped fishing; their nets hang drying on the existing net_rack props. Anyone who steps onto the platform is attacked.

The fight: Kaito is not there to kill the 'monster'. Its strength is exhausted (beached, flopping), and then the finisher pulls the stake out. The ink flakes off and the koi turns pure white. It swims up the falls and, at the lip, becomes Mizuchi: a golden dragon that rises toward the moon. The seal, now glowing clean cyan, falls onto the platform for Kaito.

Theme: the game's line is 'el camino ninja no se recorre solo' (the ninja path is not walked alone). The koi failed alone for centuries and only rises because someone helped it. That is the opposite of Kage, who chose to walk alone.

Optional reveal (recommended): the Bandana Spirit, the golden dragon in the HUD, was itself a koi that climbed these falls long ago with the grandfather's help. That explains why the bandana's spirit is a dragon and turns the HUD dragon into a character.

look:
Proportions (prototype built and rendered in Blender: scratchpad/phaseA/boss-water-0/koi_proto.py, renders2/*.png, poses_sheet.png):
- Length: 7.5 m from snout to the tips of the tail fan. Body (snout to the base of the tail) 5.7 m.
- Girth: 1.95 m wide x 1.95 m tall, reached 1.1 m behind the head.
- Spans: pectoral fins 4.7 m, tail fan 3.1 m.
- Height: model bounds 3.01 m (pelvic fin tips at 0.42 m, dorsal top at 3.43 m).
- Hover: the belly floats 0.76 m above the deck. The body axis is at 1.62 m (about Kaito's head height) and the back at 2.7 m.
- Against Kaito (1.5 m): five times his length, twice his height. On the 19.6 m platform it still leaves about 6 m of free deck on each side.

Caricature anatomy (the design doc asks for 'caricature anatomy with readable details'):
- Head is 27% of body length (a real koi is about 20%), with a chunky humped back and a short body.
- Oversized 'butterfly' (hirenaga) fins.
- A twin fan tail splayed 55 degrees from vertical. In the prototype top view a real vertical koi tail is only a 4 cm line, so splaying it makes it read as a wide fan from the camera.

Parts:
- Body loft of 16 sides x 22 rings. Every other ring is twisted half a step, so the flat facets form diamond scales; the low-poly faceting is the scale pattern.
- Protrusible lip ring (real carp shoot their mouth forward to feed), 2 gold eyes, 2 gill plates, 2 pairs of barbels.
- Long pleated pectoral fans. Under flat shading the pleats show as alternating light and dark fin rays.
- Pelvic and anal fins, a long ragged dorsal sail and the twin fan tail.
- A shimenawa rope belt with 3 paper streamers (shide) per side.
- On the back, the iron stake topped by the Water Seal medallion (key_seal_lake design x2.5, radius 0.34 m).

Palette (existing nindo_palette names only; no new swatches):
- Phase 1 'Tancho': body scales alternate white #f4f4f0 and plaster #e6dcc8; belly plaster_shade #bfb39c.
- One red disc on top of the head (flower_red #d6453a, about 0.9 m across). It is the head and bite-direction marker and the only red on the body.
- 'Gin-rin' sparkle scales: glow_moon #cfe6ff emissive on about 3.5% of the upper scales, so it glitters like the lake's sparkling facets.
- Fins: pleats in water_foam #cfe7ec / white, with only the outer 10% rim in glow_water #7ff0e0 emissive. The prototype showed fully glowing fins overpower everything.
- Eyes gold #d9a93a with black #1c1c20 pupils; mouth clay_dark #7a4a30; barbels plaster_shade.
- Rope #c9b27a / straw #d2bd80; shide paper #efe3c6; stake iron #4a4d52.
- Medallion: gold rim, water_deep #1f4a5e centre, glow_purple #c08aff corruption glow plus a pulsing 1.5-intensity purple point light, which marks the boss in the dark.
- Phase 2 'corrupted': body ink #22252a / cloth_black #26262c; belly stone_dark #5f615f / rock_dark #55575e; crack veins radiating from the stake in glow_purple; eyes glow_red #ff4a3a; coral horns (1 m) in wood_red_dark #6e1d1b with glow_red tips; long whiskers (3.2 m) in glow_purple; a taller, bristling dorsal mane; fins ink / cloth_purple #5b3a6b with a glow_purple rim. White to black-and-purple is the strongest phase change you can read from above (prototype koi_hero_p2.png).
- Freed (ending only): the phase-2 shape (horns and whiskers, so a dragon) drawn with the existing FXMaterials.Ghost additive material tinted glow_spirit #ffd86b: a golden dragon like the HUD.

Materials:
- Same as the props: the Nindo palette atlas with 2 slots (Nindo_Palette, Nindo_Emissive), flat shading, no textures, so it batches with the world.
- HitFlash and CharacterFactory.Tint still work. LiftBlacks only nudges the phase-2 ink slightly, which helps it read.

Poly budget (team characters measured by importing their FBX):
- Kaito 6,100 tris / 62 bones; ninja 6,022 / 65; Gorō 7,477 / 65; grandpa 6,973 / 82.
- Target: Body_P1 about 2,700 tris and Body_P2 about 3,100 tris. Only one is visible at a time; 5,800 in the file. 39 bones.
- The prototype at minimum density was 772 / 808 tris.

Readability (proposed arena camera at 27 m, FOV 30, 1080p, about 75 px per metre at the focus):
- Koi 380-560 px long, tancho disc about 65 px, fin blades about 150 px, Kaito about 110 px.
- Four reads from above: the red disc (head, bite direction); two pale blade fins; the wide fan tail; the glowing purple seal on the back (the curse and the finisher point).
- Each state has its own silhouette at game scale (poses_sheet.png): straight = neutral; C-curl = bite wind-up; S-shape = strike; tight C = tail whip; detached shadow = leap; on its side = beached.
- Ground anchor: a 'water mirror' ripple decal (radius 2.5 m, glow_water at 30% alpha) under the root, plus the real shadow, so the hover height reads from the high camera.
rig:
Built entirely by script (new Tools/Blender/characters/build_mizuchi.py; the prototype koi_proto.py in the scratch dir already does steps 1-3 at low density). It is deterministic and uses no auto-weights.

1. Bones from a table:
- Each entry gives head, tail and parent; edit_bones are created with roll 0 and use_connect False.
- Every chain bone lies along ±Y, so its local Z is about world up. That gives a single convention for all poses and for the Unity procedural layer: yaw = local Z rotation, pitch = local X, roll = local Y.
- The front chain points -Y (toward the head) and the back chain points +Y.
- One prototype bug, now fixed: a C-curl needs opposite signs on the front and back chains (front +a, back -a). Using the same sign gives an S.

2. Mesh:
- Built with bmesh into two objects, Body_P1 and Body_P2. The seal parts are inside both and skinned to 'seal'.
- Each vertex is weighted when it is created, through the bmesh deform layer:
  - Spine: smoothstep blend between the two nearest spine-bone centres along Y (head -2.0, spine_f -0.9, body -0.05, b1 0.62, b2 1.35, b3 2.0, b4 2.5, tail 2.95).
  - Fins: by t along the fin (bone1 = 1 - 1.4t, bone2 = 1.4t; the third bone takes t > 0.7).
  - Lips: 70% jaw / 30% head.
  - Barbel and horn segments: rigid.
  - Dorsal: spine weight x (1 - t) + dorsal bone x t.
  - Stake and medallion: 100% 'seal'.

3. Armature modifier, then parent the meshes to the armature.

Hierarchy (39 bones; Blender metres, head -> tail):
- root (0,0,0)->(0,0.6,0). Gameplay origin on the deck. Clips never translate it horizontally.
- body (0,-0.35,1.62)->(0,0.25,1.62). Centre of gravity: hover bob, roll, pitch, the 360-degree whip spin, lunges up to 1.2 m.
- Front, under body:
  - spine_f (0,-0.35,1.62)->(0,-1.35,1.62)

      - gill_L (0.7,-1.5,1.5)->(0.85,-1.1,1.4); gill_R mirrored. Breathing and roar flare.
      - horn_L (0.32,-1.75,2.2)->(0.6,-0.8,3.2); horn_R mirrored. Phase-2 mesh only.

    - pec_L1 (0.72,-1.15,1.12)->(1.45,-0.75,0.92) -> pec_L2 ->(2.0,-0.35,0.82) -> pec_L3 ->(2.35,-0.05,0.75); pec_R1-R3 mirrored.

  - dorsal_1 (0,-0.7,2.6)->(0,-0.7,3.2)

  - spine_b1 (0,0.25,1.62)->(0,1.0,1.63) -> spine_b2 ->(0,1.7,1.65) -> spine_b3 ->(0,2.3,1.67) -> spine_b4 ->(0,2.75,1.69) -> tail ->(0,3.1,1.71)

Facing guard (so the Kaito-runs-sideways bug cannot repeat):
- Before exporting, the script asserts that head.tail.y < tail.tail.y and that eye_glint.y < 0, i.e. the head points to -Y.
- With axis_forward '-Z' and axis_up 'Y', Blender -Y becomes Unity +Z (nindo_lib.blender_to_unity_vec = [-x, z, -y]), so modelYaw = 0.
- Check in Unity with the existing facing contact sheet: the tancho disc must point to +Z when the transform yaw is 0.

Export:
- One FBX: Nindo/Assets/Nindo/Art/Models/Characters/Mizuchi.fbx, containing the armature, Body_P1 and Body_P2.
- Settings: object_types {ARMATURE, MESH}, use_armature_deform_only, add_leaf_bones False, primary_bone_axis 'Y', secondary_bone_axis 'X', apply_unit_scale, apply_scale_options 'FBX_SCALE_UNITS', mesh_smooth_type 'FACE', bake_anim True, bake_anim_use_all_actions True (every action becomes a take 'MizuchiRig|<Clip>'), bake_anim_use_nla_strips False, bake_anim_force_startend_keying True, bake_anim_step 1, bake_anim_simplify_factor 0.0.
- export_grandpa.py uses a simplify factor of 0.5, which would soften the 2-frame snaps.
- Write a sidecar Mizuchi.fbx.json {clips:[{name, take, first, last, loop}]}, the same pattern as Grandpa.fbx.json.
- Unity import: Generic (animationType 2), no root motion. Use Keyframe Reduction with rotation error of 0.2 degrees or less, or no compression, so the snaps survive.

Unity procedural layer (new KoiBody.cs):
- Runs in LateUpdate after the Animator and is purely additive.
- Each bone's axis is computed as Quaternion.Inverse(bone.rotation) * Vector3.up, so it does not depend on the FBX bone axes.
- Spine-follow: keep 1 s of root-yaw history. spine_b1..tail get yaw(t - 0.05(i+1)) - yaw(t), clamped to ±30 degrees, with weights 0.35 / 0.5 / 0.65 / 0.8 / 0.9 times the locomotion weight. Turns bend the body and the tail follows the head's path.
- Bank: roll = clamp(yawRate x 0.08, ±20 degrees).
- Head look-at toward Kaito within ±25 degrees (head 0.6, spine_f 0.4) during Locomotion and Guard.
- All weights fade to 0 within 0.1 s during attack steps, so authored strikes are never altered.
- The same component handles the phase-1/phase-2 renderer swap and the 'water mirror' decal.
animations:
20 clips at 30 fps, keyed by script (new mizuchi_anims.py).

How they are authored:
- A small pose library ({bone: (rx, ry, rz)} in degrees, bone-local) and a per-clip key list [(frame, pose, interp)].
- Interpolation presets: 'snap' = EXPO ease-out, 'settle' = BACK ease-out (1.2), 'hold' = SINE in-out, 'ease' = QUAD in-out. The FBX bake samples every frame, so these curve shapes survive.
- Three procedural layers are baked on top of the keys:
  (a) Travelling wave on the spine, phase step 0.9 rad per bone from head to tail. Head amplitude is small and the tail amplitude large, the real carangiform swimming envelope.
  (b) Spring-damper secondary motion on pec_*2/3, pel_*, dorsal_*, anal, fluke_* and barbel_* (k = 60, c = 8). It is simulated frame by frame from each parent's angular acceleration and then keyed. This gives every clip automatic overlap and follow-through, so fins and whiskers never look stiff.
  (c) A noise layer for 'moving holds' and roars.

Quality rules, printed by a validation step:
- Contact frame = round(activeStart x frames) for every attack.
- Parryable attacks split anticipation / strike / recovery about 55 : 8 : 37.
- Main-bone snaps last 2-3 frames; children trail by 1-2 frames.
- Holds are never frozen (±1-2 degree tremble).
- 'root' never moves horizontally; 'body' moves at most 1.2 m.
- Each clip renders top-view and game-camera contact sheets, like scratchpad/clips/*.png.

1. Hover: 2.0 s, 60 f, loop.
- Pectoral fins 'row' ±18 degrees, alternating left/right with a 0.5 s offset (real fish hold position this way).
- Wave yaw amplitudes: spine_f 2, head -1.5 (counter-yaw keeps the eye steady, like a real fish), b1 3, b2 5, b3 8, b4 10, tail 13, plus spring on the flukes.
- Body bob ±0.10 m and pitch ±2 degrees; gills pulse 12 degrees every 2 s; dorsal ripple ±6 degrees; barbels drift (spring).

2. Swim: 1.0 s, 30 f, loop.
- Wave x1.8 (tail 24 degrees), body pitch -4 degrees, pectorals swept back 30 degrees with ±6 degree flutter, bob ±0.05 m, flukes spread 10 degrees wider.
- One tail beat per second at runSpeed 5 m/s.

3. Bite: 1.10 s, 33 f. Anticipation f0-17, strike f17-19, contact f19 (aStart 0.58), recovery f19-33.
- f0-7 settle: body sinks 0.12 m, gills flare 15 degrees, mouth shut.
- f7-13 C-curl: spine_f +26, head +22 yaw / +12 pitch (pulled back and up); b2..tail curl -20 to -35 to the same side; pectorals flare forward 40 degrees (braking); barbels trail.
- f13-17 moving hold (the telegraph pause lands here); cue at contact - 0.33 s.
- f17-19 S-snap (EXPO): front chain to -8, back chain to +10..+22, body +0.6 m forward, fins slam flat.
- f19 contact: jaw slides forward 0.28 m and opens 30 degrees; barbels whip back.
- f19-26 follow-through: the S-wave runs to the tail (tail +30 at f23); the jaw 'gulps' shut at f25 with 5 degrees of overshoot.
- f26-33: BACK ease back to hover.

4. FinL: 0.90 s, 27 f. Anticipation f0-13, strike f13-15, contact f15 (aStart 0.55), recovery f15-27.
- f0-7: roll right 35 degrees; pec_L1 +55 degrees up; pec_L2/L3 fold (scale X 0.6), so the fan closes into a blade; head turns 10 degrees toward the target.
- f7-13 moving hold, cue on the pec_L3 tip.
- f13-15 sweep: body roll snaps to -25 degrees; pec_L1 sweeps 150 degrees horizontally; the fan opens mid-sweep (scale X 1.2).
- f15-19: 15 degree overshoot plus 20 degrees of body yaw.
- f19-27: settle, ending rolled -15 degrees, which cocks the right fin.

5. FinR: 0.80 s, 24 f. Contact f10 (aStart 0.42), no hold.
- Mirror of FinL, starting from that cocked pose. The rhythm is FinL contact, then FinR contact 0.77 s later.

6. TailWhip: 1.40 s, 42 f. Anticipation f0-21, hold f12-21, strike f21-29, contact f23 (aStart 0.55), recovery f29-42.
- f0-12 coil: body +0.5 m up; front +30 / back -28 to -35 (tight C, head looking back over its shoulder at Kaito); flukes spread x1.3 and lifted 25 degrees.
- f12-21 moving hold with dripping water; cue on the fluke_L2 tip.
- f21-29 whip: body yaw +360 degrees at 60 degrees per frame; the back chain lags 2 frames, so the fan sweeps a full disc.
- f29-34: +20 degree overshoot and counter-wobble.
- f34-42: settle.

7. Spit: 1.20 s, 36 f. Release f20 (aStart 0.55).
- f0-10: rear up 30 degrees, gills puff 25 degrees, mouth opens slowly.
- f10-18: inhale (body scale x1.06).
- f20: head snaps down 15 degrees with a 35 degree jaw pop; the pearls spawn.
- f22-28: recoil 0.3 m.
- f28-36: settle.

8. Jet: 2.20 s, 66 f. Fire f36 (aStart 0.55) to f50 (aEnd 0.75).
- f0-18: rises to pitch +65 degrees, tail curls under, pectorals spread as stabilisers.
- f18-34: inhale, body swells x1.08.
- f26: the line locks.
- f34-36: head dips -50 degrees to aim.
- f36-50: jaw open 40 degrees, whole body vibrates (±2 degrees at 15 Hz), recoil 0.5 m.
- f50-66: exhale and collapse back to hover.

9. Dive: 0.80 s, 24 f.
- f0-8: turn and coil toward the rail.
- f8-14: spring up 0.5 m, pitch -45 degrees.
- f14-24: plunge at pitch -80 degrees, fins tucked. Code hides the model at f22 under a splash.

10. BreachAir: 1.10 s, 33 f, time-scaled to the actual airtime.
- f0-6: erupts nose-up 60 degrees, pectorals spread up 50 degrees like wings.
- f6-20: the 'Dragon Gate' arch at the apex (body arched, front +15 / back -15 pitch), slow 30 degree roll.
- f20-33: dives -50 degrees, mouth open, ready for the belly-flop.

11. BreachLand: 1.80 s, 54 f.
- f0: impact squash (body scale 1.18 wide, 0.82 tall).
- f0-3: rebound stretch.
- f3-12: falls onto its side (roll 80 degrees).
- f12-40: three flops (tail and head alternate, 30 -> 15 degrees, 0.3 s each); gills gasp; jaw gulps.
- f40-54: rights itself (EXPO) and does a 3-frame shake-off.

12. ClimbFalls: 1.20 s, 36 f, loop.
- Pitch +80 degrees, strong wave (tail 30 degrees, 0.6 s period), pectorals pulsing. Code moves the root up the curtain.

13. GreatWave: 1.60 s, 48 f. Slam f17 (aStart 0.35).
- f0-16: the tail fan rises out of the water, body pitch -70 degrees.
- f17: slams down 90 degrees in 2 frames.
- f19-48: sinks back.

14. Roar: 1.60 s, 48 f.
- f0-10: rears back 25 degrees.
- f10-34: jaw 45 degrees, gills 30 degrees, whiskers splay, fins fully spread, dorsal raised, shudder (noise 3 degrees at 12 Hz).
- f34-48: settle.
- Used for Spotted, the phase changes, and while hanging in the falls during the pillar attack (loops f14-30).

15. Intro: 3.00 s, 90 f.
- f0-20: erupts from the plunge pool with a 180 degree roll.
- f20-50: arc with the fins as wings, silhouetted against the falls.
- f50-60: lands into hover with a bounce.
- f60-90: turns to Kaito, flares the fins, short roar.

16. Hit: 0.45 s, 14 f.
- f0-2: jolts 12 degrees yaw and 8 degrees roll away from the hit, fins flare.
- f2-14: BACK-ease return.

17. Parried: 0.70 s, 21 f.
- f0-3: head knocked back and up (pitch +25, yaw 15); body slides back 0.6 m; jaw clacks shut; fins splay.
- f3-12: dazed wobble that dies down over 3 cycles.
- f12-21: recover.

18. Guard: 1.20 s, 36 f, holds the last pose.
- Body yaw 70 degrees to show the armoured flank, roll 20 degrees toward Kaito, fins flat, tail curled.
- The gin-rin scales flash when a hit is guarded.

19. Exhausted (Beached): 2.40 s, 72 f, loop.
- Lies on its side on the deck (body -0.8 m, roll 85 degrees), flops every 0.8 s with shrinking amplitude, gills at 2 Hz, eye roll.
- This is the punish window and the finisher pose: a fish out of water.

20. Freed: 4.00 s, 120 f.
- f0-20: rigid arch, fins spread.
- f20-40: the stake is ejected (seal bone +1.5 m, spinning, scale 0 at f40).
- f40-70: relaxes. Code swaps the phase-2 mesh to phase 1 under a white flash with ink-flake particles.
- f70-120: slow vertical swim pose. Code carries it up the falls.

Controller: Locomotion blend Hover (0) -> Swim (1) on the Speed parameter (CharacterAnimator.SetLocomotion). One state per remaining clip, same names; Idle = Hover.
moveset:
How the player reads attacks (this grammar can be reused for every boss):
- Parryable: the striking part makes a big pose change you can read from above (C-curl, roll, rear-up), then a 0.15-0.3 s 'moving hold'.
- Then, exactly 0.33 s before contact: a white glint on the striking bone (AttackDef.strikeBone) and a high 'water-chime shing'.
- Why 0.33 s: parryWindow is 0.24 s and perfectWindow 0.11 s, so a reaction of 0.10-0.33 s succeeds, and a reaction of 0.22-0.33 s lands a perfect parry.
- Dodge (unblockable): a red ground decal (ring, line or band) appears at least 0.9 s ahead, with a low taiko 'don' and a hiss. A red glint and a sharp 'ka!' come 0.33 s before contact. Dash i-frames are 0.02-0.24 s.
- Never from off-screen: dives and leaps choose emerge points that are inside the viewport (WorldToViewportPoint between 0.05 and 0.95).

The contact times below assume the telegraph-hold bug fix described in the implementation section.

PHASE 1 attacks:

A. Mordida (Bite). Parryable (Light).
- 'Bite' clip 1.10 s. Hit('Bite', 16 damage, activeStart 0.58, activeEnd 0.70, range 3.4, arc 70, lunge 2.2, telegraph 0.22, knockback 1.0); strikeBone 'jaw'.
- Tell: C-curl, pectorals flare forward, wet inhale sound about 0.5 s before contact.
- Contact about 0.91 s after the step starts; cue at 0.58 s.

B. Aletazo (Fin slash, left then right). Parryable (Light), a 2-hit string.
- FinL (0.90 s): 14 damage, activeStart 0.55 / activeEnd 0.68, range 3.3, arc 150, lunge 0.9, telegraph 0.15; strikeBone 'pec_L3'. Contact about 0.69 s.
- FinR (0.80 s): 14 damage, activeStart 0.42 / activeEnd 0.56, range 3.3, arc 150, lunge 0.7, no telegraph; strikeBone 'pec_R3'. Contact 0.77 s after FinL's contact.
- Tell: the koi rolls 35 degrees and its fan folds into a raised blade (big white shape from above). Rhythm: 'taa... ta'.

C. Coletazo (Tail whip). Parryable (Heavy). A positional punish.
- 'TailWhip' clip 1.40 s: 22 damage, activeStart 0.55 / activeEnd 0.72, range 4.6 from the root, arc 360, lunge 0, telegraph 0.28, knockback 2.4, tracking false; strikeBone 'fluke_L2'.
- Pattern only when Kaito is behind the koi (new field minAngle 100); cooldown 4 s.
- Tell: the koi coils into a tight C looking back over its shoulder, the fan rises, dripping water. Contact about 1.11 s.
- On hit: spray ring FX at radius 4.
- The koi turns slowly (turnSpeed 4.5), so flanking it is rewarded, but standing behind it is punished.

D. Perlas del Lago (Lake pearls). Parryable projectiles; a PERFECT parry reflects them.
- 'Spit' clip 1.20 s. New special 'pearls', specialParam 3, release at activeStart 0.55, telegraph 0.25, kind Projectile.
- 3 pearls in a ±18 degree fan, 9 m/s, hit radius 1.0, life 2.0 s, 10 damage each.
- Tell: the koi rears up, gills puff, water spirals into its mouth (the existing 'inward' FX tinted cyan). Each pearl is a glowing cyan icosphere (radius 0.35) with a trail and a small shadow under it. Optionally, a contracting white timing ring around each pearl meets it at contact.
- Normal parry pops the pearl.
- PerfectParry reflects it at 14 m/s, homing, recoloured gold (glow_spirit). When it hits the koi: owner.ReceiveHit(8 damage, kind Ability, which bypasses its hyper armour) plus owner.OnParried(false), i.e. +1 imbalance and a recoil.
- Dash passes through the pearl.
- This attack teaches the perfect parry.
- Pattern: minRange 5, maxRange 14, cooldown 5.

E. Salto del Dragón (Dragon-Gate leap). Unblockable, dodge with dash.
- Step 1 'Dive' (0.80 s, special 'dive'): at 0.6 the koi arcs over the nearest railing into the lake. The model is hidden under a splash. A glowing silhouette (ghost material, 1 m under the transparent water) plus a V-shaped foam wake and bubbles travels along the water ring (radius 12 m) for 1.2 s to an on-screen emerge point opposite Kaito.
- Step 2 'BreachAir' (special 'breach', radius 3.6): a 4 m splash column, then a parabola (apex 6.5 m, 1.1 s airtime) to Kaito's position plus 0.4 s of his velocity.
  - The red ring decal appears at the breach and fills over the 1.1 s; the koi's growing shadow sits inside it.
  - Landing: 30 damage, knockback 3.2, shockwave, splash and a creak of the platform planks.
- Step 3 'BreachLand' (1.8 s, no damage): beached flopping, about 1.6 s of free hits.
- Pattern cooldown 12, any range.

F. Chorro de la Cascada (Water jet). Unblockable line.
- 'Jet' clip 2.20 s. New special 'jet', specialParam 11 (line length), half-width 0.75 m; activeStart 0.55 to activeEnd 0.75 (0.44 s of jet); telegraph 0.3; 26 damage; knockback 2.6.
- The koi tracks Kaito until activeStart - 0.15. At that moment the line decal turns from faint cyan to bright red with a 'lock' click; Kaito then has about 0.75 s to step aside or dash.
- Beam: an 8-sided cylinder (radius 0.6) using the waterfall shader, scrolling at 30 m/s, with an end splash and a wet streak left on the deck.
- Pattern: minRange 4, maxRange 11, cooldown 9.

PHASE 2 additions (minPhase 1):

G. Torrente (string). Bite -> FinL -> FinR -> TailWhip (delayed variant, telegraph 0.45 with a distinct wood-creak cue).
- Contact times: 0.91 s, then 0.69 s, then 0.37 s, then 1.28 s.
- The delayed last hit punishes parry spamming (spamPenalty), but it still has its own cue.

H. Perlas de la tormenta (storm pearls). 5 pearls at ±30 degrees, released 0.15 s apart. 'Return all five' is the skill moment.

I. Chorro barrido (sweeping jet). Special 'jetsweep': the locked line rotates 70 degrees toward Kaito's side over activeStart 0.55 to activeEnd 0.82. Dash through it.

J. Ola de Kanagawa (Great Wave). Unblockable sweep.
- Steps: Dive, then 'GreatWave' (special 'greatwave', speed 8), then 'surface' (re-emerges, no damage).
- 1.2 s before the wave launches, water rises along one edge: a spray curtain along the railing, a rumble, and a red band decal.
- Then a low-poly Hokusai curl (22 m wide, 2.6 m tall, 1.2 m thick, foam 'claws') rolls across the deck at 8 m/s.
- Hit test: the wave front sweeps past Kaito (lateral check within half-width). 24 damage, knockback 3 in the wave's direction.
- Dashing through it gives 'Instante sombra' (OnDodged treats any Unblockable dodge as perfect).
- Cooldown 15.

K. Pilares de la cascada (Falls pillars). Unblockable sequence; this is where the waterfall's water reaches the gameplay frame.
- Steps: 'ClimbFalls' (special 'climb'), then 'Roar' (special 'pillars', specialParam 4), then BreachAir, then BreachLand.
- The koi swims into the main curtain and up to 14 m. It shows as a silhouette through the translucent sheet at the top of the screen, and the camera eases 8 degrees upward for 1.5 s.
- 4 falling columns. Positions: Kaito's position, then 0.6 s-ahead predictions at least 3 m apart.
- Each column: a ring decal (radius 2.2) fills over 0.9 s, then an 18 m column of falling water crashes in 0.35 s. 20 damage, knockback 2.5. Spaced 0.45 s apart.
- Then the koi itself comes down as a breach onto Kaito, and is beached for 1.6 s.
- Cooldown 20 (12 in phase 3).

phases:
Phase 1, 'El Gran Koi' (100% -> 55%)
- White Tancho look.
- Patterns A-F; attackCooldown (0.8, 1.6).
- Falls at intensity 1.0; music boss_lake layer 1 (taiko heartbeat, koto 'dripping' ostinato, shakuhachi).
- Teaches the bite rhythm, flanking (tail whip), perfect parry (pearls) and dash (leap, jet).

Transition (about 5.5 s; Mizuchi overrides Boss.PhaseChange, which must become protected virtual)
- t0: health crosses 55%. Imbalance resets to 0. The seal flares purple (flash light plus shockwave; Kaito is pushed back 3 m if within 5 m). 'Roar'. Game.InCutscene is on (Kaito invulnerable).
- t1.6: 'Dive' toward the falls. Camera shot: pitch 28, distance 32, focus moving up the curtain; this is the first full view of the waterfall during gameplay.
- t2.2-3.6: 'ClimbFalls' up to 24 m. A purple lightning bolt from the lip strikes it (flash plus thunder).
- t3.6-4.3: it falls back into the plunge pool. A big splash covers the swap from the phase-1 mesh to the phase-2 mesh.
- t4.3-5.5: the corrupted Mizuchi breaches out (Intro-like arc), lands at the arena centre and roars. Toast: '¡El sello corrompe a Mizuchi!'.
- Falls surge to intensity 1.4: faster flow, more mist and spray, deck drizzle doubled, gusts every 4-7 s. Music layer 2: heavier taiko and a shō-like choir cluster.

Phase 2, 'Mizuchi corrompido' (55% -> 25%)
- Black-and-purple look, horns, 3.2 m whiskers.
- Patterns G-K added; Mordida y aletazo, Perlas and Chorro removed (maxPhase 0).
- attackCooldown x0.7; ScaleSteps(1.1 damage, 1.12 speed); turnSpeed 6; exhaustedTime 2.8.

Phase 3, 'Desesperación' (25% -> 0%; phaseThresholds {0.55, 0.25}; generic short PhaseChange)
- 1.6 s roar, falls surge to 1.6, Pilares cooldown 20 -> 12, phaseSpeedBonus 0.08.
- Music: double-time taiko.

Finisher and ending
- FinisherAllowed at 12% or less, while beached (exhausted) or at low health. The 'EJECUTAR' prompt appears over the seal on its back.
- Kaito's Finisher clip plays; Execute calls Die(finisher).
- MizuchiBoss overrides DeathRoutine, which must become protected virtual. Instead of tipping over and shrinking, it plays the 6 s ascension:
  1. 'Freed': the stake cracks and is ejected.
  2. Ink flakes burst off and the phase-2 mesh swaps to phase 1 under a white flash; the koi is pure white with a gold rim glow.
  3. It swims to the falls and climbs the curtain. Camera: low shot from the platform tilting up.
  4. At the lip (t 5.2) it bursts into the golden dragon: phase-2 shape with the gold ghost material and a long particle ribbon, and flies into the moon.
  5. The camera returns to normal.
- Toast 'Mizuchi, liberado'. OnDeathFinished (overridden) spawns KeyPickup(SealId.Lago) at the arena centre, because the koi is now at the top of the falls. Falls calm to 0.8; lake fog -20%; shrine lanterns on.

Retry
- ResetEnemy restores the phase-1 mesh, falls intensity 1.0, and puts the koi back on the arena NavMesh (agent re-enabled, warped to spawn).
- Every off-arena coroutine (dive, climb, breach) is stopped by StopAllCoroutines in ResetEnemy, which is already called.

Key measurement (Blender layout render, scratchpad/phaseA/boss-water-0/camera_compare.png and renders2/L_*.png):

Falls (geometry generated at runtime by WaterfallFX.cs from waterfall descriptors in the prop manifest, set with mb.set('waterfalls', [...]); WorldBuilder applies the prop transform via blender_to_unity_vec):
1. Main 'Devil's Throat' curtain: follows the arc from 45 to 135 degrees, so it is curved and its ends come toward the camera.
- 24 columns x 16 rows. Lip from 30 m at the ends to 42 m at the centre. 1.2 m/s outward speed at the lip with true ballistic rows (z = h - 4.9t²), so the plunge line sits at radius 11 from (0, 2): about 3.2 m behind the platform's back edge at the centre and about 2 m at its corners.
- Vertex colours: R = fall progress, G = edge factor, B = per-column random.
2. Side ribbons: θ = 25 / 155 degrees, 4 m wide, about 22 m tall, at (±13.1, 8.1). These are the falls that stay in the upper corners of the gameplay frame. Plus 2 trickles at θ = 15 / 165 degrees (2 m wide, about 19.5 m).

Shader 'Nindo/Waterfall Lowpoly' (URP; transparent queue 'Transparent-5'; cull off; zwrite off; same faceted language as NindoWater.shader):
- Vertex:
  - Bulges along the sheet normal, sin(sqrt(R) x 9 - t x _FlowSpeed x 6 + B x 6.28) x lerp(0.05, 0.4, R): bulges that speed up as they fall.
  - Wind sway on x: sin(t x 0.7 + y x 0.05) x 0.3 x R.
- Fragment:
  - Flat facet normals from ddx/ddy.
  - Streaks: s = frac(sqrt(R) x _StreakScale(6) - t x _FlowSpeed + B). Using sqrt(R) makes the streaks accelerate like free fall (v = √(2gh)).
  - Foam where s < lerp(0.15, 0.75, R): water aerates and whitens as it falls.
  - Colour: lip band (R < 0.06) glassy water_deep #1f4a5e with a moon-specular line; mid section water_shallow #3f7f8f; foam #e8f4f6.
  - Moon facet specular and sparkles like the lake shader.
  - Emission = foam x 0.25 x #cfe6ff, so the falls read at night.
  - Alpha = lerp(0.92, 0.55, G); ragged sides via clip(alpha - noise(G)); fog.
- Properties: _FlowSpeed (1, 1.4 in phase 2), _Turbulence, _CorruptTint (purple near the lip during the phase change and Pilares), _Intensity.
- Fallback if it does not compile: an unlit transparent material with a scrolling texture, as the water already does.

Particles (Shuriken built in code like FXFactory, under one WaterfallFX root; max about 1,600 alive):
1. Falling clumps: rate 45/s along the lip, forward 1.2 ±0.3 m/s, gravityModifier 1.0, life 2.95 s (= √(2 x 42 / 9.81)), stretched billboards (velocityScale 0.05, lengthScale 2), white. Real ballistics, so they visibly accelerate.
2. Plunge boil: mesh particles (icosphere subdiv 1, 20 tris) lit with the palette material, so they are faceted foam chunks lit by the moon. Box 26 x 0.5 x 2 m on the plunge arc, 110/s, life 0.7-1.3 s, 3-7 m/s up in a 30 degree cone, gravity 0.9, size 0.5-1.6, size over life 0.6 -> 1.4, white -> water_foam.
3. Rolling mist: soft billboards (FXMaterials.SoftDot), alpha blended. 14/s, life 5-8 s, size 5-10 (x2.2 over life), 1.5-3.5 m/s up plus a velocity over lifetime of 1.2 m/s toward the arena and 0.8 m/s up. Noise module: strength 0.8, frequency 0.12, scroll 0.3 for curling. Alpha 0 -> 0.16 -> 0, colour #b9c7d8, at most 110 alive.
4. Wind-driven spray: 260/s, life 2.5-4.5 s, 6-10 m/s up in a 25 degree cone, gravity 0.35, External Forces from a local WindZone (directional toward the arena, 2 m/s, turbulence 1.5, pulse 0.3 Hz). Size 0.03-0.07, stretched, additive glow_moon at 40%. This is the glittering drizzle that crosses the gameplay frame.
5. Deck splashes: horizontal ring billboards on a 10 m disc at deck height. 30/s (60/s in phase 2), life 0.35 s, size 0.1 -> 0.45, alpha 0.5 -> 0, with a sub-emitter of 3 droplet sparks. Kaito fights on a wet, living floor.
6. Foam rings: horizontal ring meshes every 0.25 s along the plunge line, expanding to radius 4-6 m over 3.5 s and drifting 1.0 m/s toward the arena (riding the outflow) until they reach the platform piles.
7. Outflow foam ribbons: 2 static UV-scrolling strips (3 m wide, 1.2 m/s, alpha 0.35) that split around the platform and flow southwest past the boardwalk.
8. Lip spill: 60/s, 1.2 s life (cutscene detail).
9. Moonbow (polish): a flat torus strip (radius 22, 120 degrees, 1.5 m wide) in the mist above the plunge. Desaturated spectrum with a white core, additive at 10%. Real moonbows form in waterfall mist under moonlight.
- Gust controller: every 7-11 s (4-7 s in phase 2), spray and mist x1.8 and WindZone x2 for 1.8 s, deck drizzle x2, 'whoosh' sound. Surge(float) API for the phase change and Pilares (x2.5).
- Distance LOD: emitters off beyond 110 m from Kaito. On Low quality, rates are halved and layer 4 is off.

6. Enemy.TickAttack fixes. These affect every enemy and target the user's 'I can't tell when to parry' complaint, so coordinate with whoever owns combat:
- (a) Telegraph hold bug (Enemy.cs:448). holdEnd = telegraph + (activeStart - 0.12) * stepLen assumes the wind-up plays at speed 1, but the Snappy curve plays it at 0.85. The real hold is therefore telegraph - 0.176*(activeStart - 0.12)*stepLen.
  - Gorō's 'Golpe sísmico' (Heavy, 2.967 s, activeStart 0.55, telegraph 0.3) actually holds 0.075 s.
  - Gorō's Combo1 holds 0.124 s instead of 0.2 s.
  - Fix: record the time stepNorm first reaches activeStart - 0.12, and hold until that time + telegraph. EstimateStrikeEta must use the same rule.
- (b) Glint (Enemy.cs:461) fires at normalized activeStart - 0.18, so its lead in seconds changes with every clip. Fire it when strikeEta <= 0.33f instead (const GlintLead), and play the 'tell_parry' or 'tell_danger' sound there.
- (c) Add 'protected virtual bool StepHeld => false' in TickAttack: no stepNorm advance or anim speed while held. The dive, climb and pillar specials wait on their coroutines with it.

F. Risks
1. Off-NavMesh coroutines (dive, breach, climb) leaving the agent disabled after a death or retry. Mitigation: reset in ResetEnemy, StopAllCoroutines, failsafe warp.
2. A single capsule hurtbox on a 7.5 m body: hits on the tail beyond 3.6 m from the root will not register. Mitigation: radius 1.3, the attack magnet (4.5 m), the root placed at the pectorals. Optionally a second hurt sphere at spine_b3.
3. The camera yaw change near the arena may disorient. It blends smoothly and only applies within 24 m, which mostly covers the platform and the last boardwalk stretch.
4. Mist overdraw on low-end GPUs: cap the count and size, use quality tiers.
5. Unity animation compression smoothing the 2-frame snaps: set the rotation error low or turn compression off.
6. NormalizeHeight measures every renderer, hidden ones included: keep the phase-2 horns and whiskers inside the phase-1 bounds (horn top 3.2 m < dorsal 3.43 m), or measure with Body_P2 disabled.
7. The lead is editing StoryText, StoryDirector and Areas right now (uncommitted changes in git status): merge the story and zone edits after theirs.
8. Fixes 6a and 6b change the timing of every existing enemy (better tells but different rhythm). Retune telegraph values for the ninja, sumo, Gorō and Kage afterwards.
